chosen.premise: Gigantamax Charizard jumps from 1.7 meters to 28 meters tall—over 16 times its normal height.
chosen.hook: Charizard can become taller than a seven-story building.
chosen.visualIdea: A 1.7 m Charizard stands beside its 28 m Gigantamax form, with stacked normal Charizards climbing to its head.
chosen.note: A highly Charizard-specific transformation with a precise 1.7 m-to-28 m comparison. The seven-story comparison is an understandable visual inference, while the height data itself is directly supported.

candidates.premise: Gigantamax Charizard jumps from 1.7 meters to 28 meters tall—over 16 times its normal height.
candidates.hook: Charizard can become taller than a seven-story building.
candidates.visualIdea: A 1.7 m Charizard stands beside its 28 m Gigantamax form, with stacked normal Charizards climbing to its head.
candidates.note: A highly Charizard-specific transformation with a precise 1.7 m-to-28 m comparison. The seven-story comparison is an understandable visual inference, while the height data itself is directly supported.

candidates.premise: Gigantamax Charizard weighs 1,000 kg, more than 11 times the 90.5 kg of normal Charizard.
candidates.hook: Charizard gains nearly a metric ton in one transformation.
candidates.visualIdea: A scale slams from 90.5 kg to 1,000 kg as normal Charizard inflates into Gigantamax Charizard.
candidates.note: The 90.5 kg-to-1,000 kg jump is exact and well supported, but weight gain is less visually intuitive and less inherently dramatic than the height transformation.

candidates.premise: Charizard seeks powerful opponents but is said to never use its fire breath on a weaker foe.
candidates.hook: Charizard hunts strong opponents—and spares the weak.
candidates.visualIdea: Charizard flies past smaller challengers, then lands before a powerful silhouette as its flames ignite.
candidates.note: The noble battle rule is distinctive and directly stated in two Pokédex entries. It is slightly less concrete than a numerical or form-based angle and depends on wording such as 'is said to.'

candidates.premise: Mega Charizard X is the one listed form that trades Flying for Dragon, becoming Fire/Dragon instead.
candidates.hook: Charizard’s Dragon form actually loses Flying.
candidates.visualIdea: Type badges flip from Fire/Flying to Fire/Dragon for Mega X, while Mega Y and Gmax retain Flying.
candidates.note: A concrete, unusual type contradiction supported by the listed forms. It is excellent for an on-screen badge comparison, though some fans may already know Mega Charizard X. (Uniqueness capped at 2: its evidence is only fields every Pokémon has.)

candidates.premise: When Charizard becomes furious, its tail flame is said to flare from red into a whitish-blue shade.
candidates.hook: Charizard’s anger has a color: blue.
candidates.visualIdea: A close-up red tail flame pulses with rage, then flashes into a pale blue blaze.
candidates.note: The red-to-whitish-blue visual is strong and supported by multiple entries, but the core fact is familiar to many fans and 'blue' simplifies the source wording.

candidates.premise: Charizard’s fire is said to get hotter through battle experience—and harsh battles intensify it further.
candidates.hook: For Charizard, battle experience is fuel.
candidates.visualIdea: Each battle adds heat to a thermometer until Charizard’s flame melts a boulder.
candidates.note: The entries support fire intensifying with experience and harsh battles, but the premise is broad and the two claims are not presented as one tightly defined mechanic.

rounds.request: Stronger alternatives would need an equally concrete transformation or contradiction, direct support in the supplied research, and a more distinctive visual payoff than Charizard growing from 1.7 to 28 meters.
